conventions: stop entries mechanized as signal-bar-close then next-bar-open; every tunable constant is a parameter; long side only in pseudocode; 'session' means the intraday trading day, first bar of the session is the bar whose Date differs from the prior bar's

candidates.name: OpeningRangeHeight
candidates.quote: The opening range usually provides clues to how the day will unfold
candidates.description: Primitive: the opening range of the session is the highest high minus the lowest low of the first N bars of the session. Exposed as a local for the other TP4 candidates; as a standalone filter it is true once N bars of the session have printed.
candidates.pseudocode: barsIntoSession = count of bars since the first bar of this Date (0-based); if (barsIntoSession < openingBars) return false; orHigh = highest(high over the first openingBars bars of the session); orLow = lowest(low over the same bars); orHeight = orHigh - orLow; return true

complexity.reason: needs session-boundary detection from the Date series and a per-session persistent high/low

notes: Brooks defines the opening range loosely ('first 30 to 60 minutes', elsewhere 'first five to 10 bars'); 12 bars = one hour of 5-minute bars.
Chapter 21 and 22 define the same primitive; dedup should merge.

candidates.name: AverageDailyRange
candidates.quote: If the opening range is about half of the range of the recent days
candidates.description: Primitive: the average of the full-session high-low range over the last D completed sessions, computed on the intraday series by tracking each session's running high and low and rolling them at the Date change.
candidates.pseudocode: on Date change: push (sessionHigh - sessionLow) into dailyRanges, reset sessionHigh/sessionLow; adr = average(dailyRanges, dailyLookback); return dailyRanges.size() >= dailyLookback

complexity.reason: cross-bar state: a per-session high/low and a ring buffer of completed session ranges

notes: Brooks says 'recent days' without a count; 5 is a reading.

candidates.name: SmallOpeningRangeBreakoutMode
candidates.quote: In general, if the opening range is small, it will be followed by a breakout.
candidates.description: Filter: the session's opening range is smaller than a fraction of the average daily range, so the day is in breakout mode and breakout entries in either direction are permitted.
notes: Brooks gives 'under 30 percent' explicitly on page 385 of chapter 21; 'small' here is read as the same threshold.

candidates.name: HalfOpeningRangeTrendingRangeDay
candidates.quote: If the opening range is about half of the range of the recent days, the breakout will often lead to a measured move and a trending trading range day.
candidates.description: Filter: the opening range is between a lower and an upper fraction of the average daily range (around one half), so a breakout is expected to travel about one opening-range height and then form a second range; entries in both directions are allowed afterwards.
candidates.pseudocode: orHeight >= lowFraction * adr && orHeight <= highFraction * adr
notes: Chapter 22 restates this as 'a third to half' and 'first hour or two', hence openingBars 24 here.

candidates.name: OpeningRangeMeasuredMoveTarget
candidates.quote: the breakout will often lead to a measured move and a trending trading range day
candidates.description: Exit: after an upside breakout of the opening range, take profit when the high reaches the opening-range high plus a multiple of the opening-range height (the measured move that roughly doubles the day's range).
candidates.book_order_type: limit order at the measured-move price (mechanized as exit at next open once touched)

complexity.reason: per-session opening range state plus a target projection

candidates.name: LargeOpeningRangeSpikeDay
candidates.quote: If the opening range is large, there is usually a spike and the day will likely become a spike and channel trend day.
candidates.description: Filter: the opening range already exceeds a large fraction of the average daily range, so the opening move is a spike; with-trend entries only (direction of the spike) for the rest of the session.
candidates.pseudocode: orHeight > largeFraction * adr && close[0] > sessionOpen  /* long side: opening spike was up */

complexity.reason: per-session state primitives plus session open

notes: Direction of the spike is taken as sign(close - session open) at the end of the opening range; Brooks does not spell this out.

candidates.name: DayTrendDirection
candidates.quote: if you recognize one as it is unfolding, you should be focusing on trading in the with-trend direction only
candidates.description: Research primitive: the direction of the day's trend, needed by every 'with-trend only' filter in Part IV. Simplest mechanization: sign of (close minus session open) once the opening range has printed, or sign of (close minus the 20-bar EMA). Long side true when the day trend is up.
candidates.pseudocode: barsIntoSession >= openingBars && close[0] > sessionOpen  /* alternative: close[0] > ema(close, emaLength) */

complexity.reason: 'the trend of the day' is a judgment; a design decision on the proxy is needed before coding

notes: Chapter 21 defines 'always-in' as the same concept; dedup should merge.

candidates.name: WithTrendOnlyOnTrendDay
candidates.quote: you should be trying to take every with-trend entry, no matter how weak the setup looks
candidates.description: Filter: when a trend-day pattern has been recognized (opening range small or large, per TP4-03/TP4-06), only allow entries in the day's trend direction. Long side: day trend is up.

complexity.reason: depends on the research-grade DayTrendDirection primitive

notes: Corollary on page 354: if no pattern is recognized, assume a trading range day and allow both directions; that is simply this filter being false.

candidates.name: BullReversalBar
candidates.quote: only if there is a good reversal bar
candidates.description: Primitive: a bull reversal bar opens near its low, closes near its high with a bull body, and has a lower tail; a 'good' one has a body of at least a fraction of its range and a close above the prior bar's close.
candidates.pseudocode: close[0] > open[0] && (close[0] - open[0]) >= bodyFraction * (high[0] - low[0]) && (open[0] - low[0]) >= tailFraction * (high[0] - low[0]) && (high[0] - close[0]) <= topTailMax * (high[0] - low[0])
notes: Brooks's reversal-bar definition is in the earlier chapters of this book; this is the working test used by Part IV.

candidates.name: TrendLineBreakOccurred
candidates.quote: you should take countertrend entries only after a trend line break
candidates.description: Filter for countertrend entries: within the last N bars, a bar closed beyond the trend line drawn through the two most recent swing lows of the bull trend (long side: a bear trend line through the last two swing highs was broken to the upside, permitting a countertrend long).
candidates.pseudocode: line = projectLine(swingHigh[2], swingHigh[1]) /* bear trend line */; any bar k in 0..withinBars with close[k] > line.at(k)

complexity.reason: needs swing-pivot detection and trend-line projection

candidates.name: CountertrendEntryRequiresReversalBar
candidates.quote: take countertrend entries only after a trend line break, only if there is a good reversal bar
candidates.description: Composite filter: a long taken against the day's trend is allowed only if a trend line break has occurred and the signal bar is a good bull reversal bar; enter at the next open after the reversal bar closes.
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the reversal bar high

candidates.name: CountertrendScalpTarget
candidates.quote: On the countertrend trades, you should scalp your entire position.
candidates.description: Exit: a position taken against the day's trend is closed as soon as open profit reaches a scalp target measured in ticks (or points); with-trend positions are not affected.
candidates.book_order_type: limit order at entry plus the scalp distance

complexity.reason: needs the day-trend direction remembered from entry time

notes: Brooks's Emini scalp is four ticks (one point) in this era; scalpTicks default from that.
Without the countertrend gate this is TakeProfit in ticks.

candidates.name: MaxCountertrendTradesPerSession
candidates.quote: you should not find more than two or three countertrend trades in the day
candidates.description: Filter: block a countertrend entry once the number of countertrend entries taken this session has reached the maximum.
candidates.pseudocode: countertrendEntriesThisSession < maxCountertrend  /* counter reset on Date change, incremented when an entry is filled against dayTrend */

complexity.reason: persistent per-session counter fed by position-history reads

candidates.name: VeryStrongTrendNoCountertrend
candidates.quote: In a very strong trend, all trades should be with-trend swings (scalping out part) and no trades should be countertrend scalps
candidates.description: Filter: when the trend is very strong (proxy: the close has stayed above the EMA for at least N consecutive bars), block any short entry; long side of the mirrored rule is 'trend is very strongly up, longs allowed'.
candidates.pseudocode: barsAboveEma = consecutive bars with close > ema(close, emaLength); barsAboveEma >= strongBars

complexity.reason: an EMA and a counter persisting between bars

notes: Chapter 21 page 365 gives the 20-bars-above-the-moving-average proxy for 'very strong'; used here as the default.

candidates.name: PatternRecognitionWindow
candidates.quote: you will find that you can see them potentially setting up in the first 30 to 60 minutes
candidates.description: Filter: the day-type classification (TP4-03/04/06) is only trusted once the session is at least M minutes old; before that, treat the day as undecided (both directions allowed, scalps only).

complexity.reason: a Time comparison against the session open time

candidates.name: SwingPartOfPositionOnTrendDay
candidates.quote: make sure to take every with-trend trade and swing part of your position
candidates.description: Exit management: on a recognized trend day, scalp out part of a with-trend position at the scalp target and hold the remainder to the session close (or until an opposite signal). If the engine trades one unit, the single-unit reading is 'hold with-trend positions to the close, no scalp exit'.
candidates.pseudocode: ctx.MarketPosition() > 0 && dayTrendUpAtEntry && (partialTaken == false && profitTicks >= scalpTicks -> exit scalpFraction of size; else hold until Time >= sessionCloseTime)
candidates.book_order_type: limit at scalp target for the scalp part; remainder held with a trailing stop

complexity.reason: partial-exit state; may need pyramiding/partial-exit support the pane system lacks

notes: Recorded because Brooks states it as a rule; whether partial exits are expressible is an authoring-pass decision.

rejected.quote: The names are meaningless because all that a trader needs to know is how to read the price action
When it happens, don't question it or be upset by it. Just accept it and trade it.

chapter_summary: Two-page introduction to Part IV. It classifies trend days by the size of the opening range relative to recent daily ranges (small -> breakout, half -> measured move and trending trading range day, large -> spike and channel) and sets trading-mode rules: with-trend only on trend days, countertrend only after a trend-line break with a good reversal bar and scalped, at most two or three countertrend trades per day. Produced the opening-range and average-daily-range primitives (all intraday-only), day-trend-direction and with-trend filters, countertrend gating filters, a countertrend scalp exit, and an opening-range measured-move exit.
